Below is a focused 3-week reconditioning block to safely restore strength, work capacity, and bodyweight after mild flu and a 3-week layoff. It emphasizes submaximal loading, volume ramp, aerobic base, and recovery. Structure is 4 lifting days + 1–2 conditioning/recovery days per week. All loads are guided by RPE; suggested percentages are anchored to pre-illness maxes but adjust daily to how he feels.

Overview
- Goals: Rebuild movement quality, tissue tolerance, and aerobic base; progress toward 80–90% of prior strength by Week 3; support weight regain.
- Split: Upper/Lower/Rest/Upper/Lower/Active Recovery/Rest (modifiable).
- Intensity: Start light (RPE 6–7), add volume before intensity, then sharpen loads in Week 3.
- Conditioning: Low- to moderate-intensity aerobic work to aid recovery and appetite; no high-intensity intervals in Weeks 1–2.
- Autoregulation: If morning fatigue, elevated RHR (>8–10 bpm), or poor sleep, reduce top set load 2–5% and trim 1 back-off set per lift.

Warm-up (each session)
- 5–8 min easy cardio (bike/row), nasal breathing.
- Dynamic mobility: T-spine rotations, hip flexor stretch, band pull-aparts, 90/90 hips, ankle rocks (4–6 reps each).
- Movement prep: 2–3 ramp-up sets per main lift, RPE 4–6.

Week 1: Reintroduce patterns, accumulate easy volume, assess fatigue
- RPE target: 6–7 throughout; stop 3–4 reps in reserve (RIR).
- Conditioning: Two sessions of Zone 2 (20–30 min), one optional 15–20 min walk.

Day 1 – Upper A
- Bench press: 4 sets x 5 reps @ ~65% (RPE 6)
- One-arm DB row: 3 x 8–10/side (RPE 7)
- Incline DB bench: 3 x 8 (RPE 7)
- Lat pulldown (neutral grip): 3 x 10 (RPE 7)
- Cable external rotation + band pull-aparts: 2 x 12–15 each
- Core: Dead bug 3 x 8/side

Day 2 – Lower A
- Back squat: 4 x 5 @ ~60–65% (RPE 6)
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8 (RPE 6–7)
- Split squat (rear-foot elevated if tolerated): 3 x 8/side (RPE 7)
- Leg curl: 3 x 10 (RPE 7)
- Standing calf raise: 3 x 12
- Breathing cooldown: 3–4 min nasal breathing, 90/90 with hip lift

Day 3 – Active Recovery
- Zone 2 cardio: 20–30 min (bike/elliptical), conversational pace.
- Mobility circuit: 10–15 min (hips, T-spine, ankles).
- Optional: 10 min walk later in day.

Day 4 – Upper B
- Overhead press (barbell or DB): 4 x 5 (RPE 6)
- Weighted pull-up or assisted: 4 x 5 (RPE 6–7) or 4 x 6–8 bodyweight if needed
- Close-grip bench or dips (assisted as needed): 3 x 8 (RPE 7)
- Chest-supported row: 3 x 8–10 (RPE 7)
- Face pulls: 2 x 12–15
- Farmer carry: 3 x 20–30 m

Day 5 – Lower B
- Deadlift (conventional): 4 x 3 @ ~65% (keep bar speed crisp; RPE 6)
- Front squat or tempo goblet squat (3-1-1): 3 x 6–8 (RPE 7)
- Hip thrust: 3 x 8 (RPE 7)
- Reverse lunge: 2–3 x 8/side
- Plank: 3 x 30–45 s

Day 6 – Optional Recovery
- 20–30 min easy walk or swim; light mobility.
Day 7 – Rest

Week 2: Build volume, introduce one heavier top set, maintain aerobic base
- RPE target: 6–8; include one top set at RPE 7–8 on main lifts, then back-off volume.
- Conditioning: Two Zone 2 sessions (25–35 min).

Day 1 – Upper A
- Bench press: Work to 1 top set x 4 @ ~70–75% (RPE 7–8), then 3 x 4 @ -8–10% load (RPE 6–7)
- One-arm DB row: 4 x 8–10 (RPE 7–8)
- Incline DB bench: 3 x 8 (RPE 7–8)
- Wide-grip pulldown or pull-ups: 3 x 8–10
- Cable Y raise + external rotations: 2 x 12–15
- Pallof press: 3 x 10/side

Day 2 – Lower A
- Back squat: Top set 1 x 4 @ ~70–75% (RPE 7–8), then 3 x 4 @ -8–10%
- RDL: 3 x 6–8 (RPE 7)
- Split squat: 3 x 8/side (RPE 7–8)
- Leg curl: 3 x 10–12
- Calf raise: 3 x 12–15

Day 3 – Active Recovery
- Zone 2: 25–35 min
- 10–15 min mobility; breath work

Day 4 – Upper B
- Overhead press: Top set 1 x 4 (RPE 7–8), then 3 x 4 back-offs
- Pull-ups: 4 x 5–6 weighted lightly if easy; otherwise bodyweight to RPE 7
- Close-grip bench or dips: 3 x 6–8 (RPE 7–8)
- Chest-supported row: 3 x 8–10
- Face pulls or rear-delt fly: 2 x 12–15
- Suitcase carry: 3 x 20–30 m/side

Day 5 – Lower B
- Deadlift: Top set 1 x 3 @ ~70–75% (RPE 7–8), then 3 x 3 @ -8–10%
- Front squat (or tempo goblet): 3 x 5–6 (RPE 7–8)
- Hip thrust: 3 x 8 (RPE 7–8)
- Reverse lunge: 2–3 x 8/side
- Stir-the-pot or ab wheel: 3 x 6–10

Day 6 – Optional Recovery
- 25–30 min easy walk or cycle; light mobility.
Day 7 – Rest

Week 3: Sharpen intensity, reduce junk volume, test proximity to baseline
- RPE target: 7–9 on top sets; crisp technique. Slight deload of accessory volume to keep CNS fresh.
- Conditioning: One Zone 2 (20–30 min) early in week only.

Day 1 – Upper A
- Bench press: Work to 1–2 top sets x 3 @ ~77–82% (RPE 8–9), then 2 x 3 @ -8–10%
- One-arm DB row: 3 x 6–8 (RPE 8)
- Incline DB bench: 2 x 6–8 (RPE 8)
- Pulldown or pull-ups: 2–3 x 6–8 (RPE 8)
- Light shoulder health: 1–2 x 12–15

Day 2 – Lower A
- Back squat: 1–2 top sets x 3 @ ~77–82% (RPE 8–9), then 2 x 3 back-offs
- RDL: 3 x 5–6 (RPE 7–8)
- Split squat: 2 x 6–8/side
- Calf raise: 2 x 10–12

Day 3 – Light Recovery
- Zone 2: 20–30 min or 20 min brisk walk
- Mobility 10 min

Day 4 – Upper B
- Overhead press: 1–2 top sets x 3 (RPE 8), then 2 x 3 back-offs
- Pull-ups: 3–4 x 5–6 (RPE 8)
- Close-grip bench or dips: 2 x 5–6 (RPE 8)
- Chest-supported row: 2 x 6–8

Day 5 – Lower B
- Deadlift: 1–2 top sets x 2–3 @ ~77–82% (RPE 8–9), then 2 x 2–3 back-offs
- Front squat: 2 x 4–5 (RPE 7–8)
- Hip thrust: 2 x 6–8 (RPE 8)
- Core: Plank 2 x 45–60 s

Day 6 – Optional Recovery
- Easy walk or off.
Day 7 – Rest

Readiness and load management
- Morning check: Resting HR, sleep duration/quality, perceived fatigue. If HR up >8–10 bpm or fatigue >7/10, reduce main lift load 2–5% and drop one back-off set.
- Bar speed: If rep 2 of a top set is grindy, stop 1–2 reps early and use that load for back-offs.

Technique cues
- Bench: Scapular retraction, consistent bar path (touch lower sternum), 1–2 s pause on first rep in Weeks 1–2 to reinforce control.
- Squat: Brace before descent, knees track over mid-foot, controlled 2–3 s eccentric in Week 1 accessories.
- Deadlift: Lats tight (“bend the bar”), press floor away, smooth lockout.

Nutrition to regain 4 kg and support recovery (3 weeks)
- Caloric surplus: +250–350 kcal/day in Week 1; +350–500 kcal/day in Weeks 2–3 if digestion and fatigue are fine. Aim to regain 0.4–0.6 kg/week.
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day across 3–5 meals; include 25–40 g high-quality protein post-workout.
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day in Week 1; 4–6 g/kg/day Weeks 2–3. Front-load carbs pre-/post-training.
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day, mostly unsaturated; include omega-3s (1–2 g EPA/DHA/day).
- Hydration/electrolytes: 30–40 ml/kg/day water; add 1–2 g sodium on training days if sweating and to support appetite/energy.
- Micronutrients: Vitamin D per status, a basic multivitamin, fruit/veg 5+ servings/day; yogurt/fermented foods for gut.

Recovery and illness-specific considerations
- Sleep: 7.5–9 h/night; optional 20–30 min nap on heavy days.
- Post-illness pacing: Avoid failure work and HIIT for first 2 weeks; prioritize Zone 2 and walks.
- Heat exposure: Optional 10–15 min mild sauna 1–2x/week if well-hydrated; skip if dizziness/fatigue worsens.
- Stop/modify if: Chest tightness, unusual breathlessness at low effort, HR not recovering between sets, or fatigue accumulates day-to-day—scale volume and notify you.

End-of-block readiness check (end of Week 3)
- Benchmark singles: After warm-ups, take single @ RPE 7–8 (~80–85%) in bench, squat, deadlift. If speed and form are solid, proceed to next block targeting 85–92+% and normal hypertrophy volume. If any lift feels off, hold one more week at Week 3 structure before ramping.

This plan restores capacity without overshooting, supports weight regain, and positions him to transition into regular strength and hypertrophy training in Week 4.

Notes

Week 3 (total run 10–12 km, approach pre-illness 10k)
- Wed: Easy run 35–40 min (RPE 3–4). ~5–6.5 km.
- Sat: Easy run 25–35 min including 4–6 x 15–20 s relaxed strides with full walk-back recovery after the main easy portion. Do not sprint; just smooth, quick mechanics.

- Use talk test or 70–78% max HR as a guide. If he used to run 10k at, say, 5:00/km, keep Week 1–2 around 5:45–6:15/km (or whatever yields conversational effort).

- Shoe/terrain: Rotate a cushioned daily trainer; avoid cambered roads early.

- Pre-run (60–90 min before): 30–60 g carbs + 10–20 g protein; hydrate with 300–500 ml water and a pinch of salt if warm out.
- Post-run: 25–40 g protein + 60–90 g carbs within 1–2 hours (can be combined with lifting nutrition if same day but spaced).

  - 1 x longer easy run (45–60 min) + 1 x shorter easy run with 6–8 strides, or
  - Consolidate into one 8–10 km easy run if time-limited, and gradually reintroduce moderate efforts/tempos in Weeks 4–5.

This gets him back to a consistent weekly 10k while protecting strength recovery after illness.

Here’s a simple, actionable intake target for 3 weeks to regain ~0.4–0.6 kg/week, restore training energy, and support recovery. Adjust weekly based on bodyweight change, appetite, GI comfort, and readiness.

Step 1: Calorie target
- Starting point: Maintenance (post-illness) is likely down. For a 41-year-old intermediate lifter back to 4 lifts + 2 easy runs/week, estimate 30–33 kcal/kg/day in Week 1.
- Surplus: Add +250–350 kcal/day in Week 1; increase to +350–500 kcal/day Weeks 2–3 if recovery is good and weight is trending up <0.4 kg/week.
- Practical targets (per kg bodyweight):
  - Week 1: 33–36 kcal/kg/day
  - Weeks 2–3: 35–38 kcal/kg/day
- Example: If he weighs 80 kg now (after -4 kg), targets are:
  - Week 1: ~2,650–2,900 kcal/day
  - Weeks 2–3: ~2,800–3,050 kcal/day
- Titrate: If scale weight doesn’t rise ~0.4–0.6 kg in a week, add +150–200 kcal/day the following week. If gain >0.8 kg/week with bloat/fatigue, trim -150–200 kcal.

Step 2: Macros
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day (aim ~2.0 g/kg).
  - 80 kg example: 145–175 g/day (target ~160 g).
- Carbohydrate: 4–6 g/kg/day; favor the higher end on lift/run days.
  - 80 kg example: 320–480 g/day (target ~360–420 g most days).
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day, primarily unsaturated.
  - 80 kg example: 65–80 g/day (target ~70–75 g).
- Macro distribution notes:
  - If appetite is low: push carbs up (easier to eat) and keep fats moderate; use liquid nutrition.
  - If GI feels sensitive post-illness: start closer to 4–5 g/kg carbs and 0.8 g/kg fat, then build.

Step 3: Peri-workout fueling
- Pre-lift (60–120 min): 30–80 g carbs + 20–40 g protein; low fat/fiber.
- Intra (optional on >75 min sessions): 20–30 g carbs + electrolytes.
- Post-lift (within 1–2 h): 30–50 g protein + 60–100 g carbs.
- Run days: Add 30–60 g carbs in the 1–2 h pre-run and 40–80 g carbs post-run (can overlap with lifting nutrition if same day).

Step 4: Meal structure
- 3–5 feedings/day, anchor protein 25–45 g each.
- Example day (80 kg, ~2,900–3,000 kcal, ~160 P / 380 C / 80 F):
  - Breakfast: 40 g protein + 90 g carbs + 20 g fat (e.g., Greek yogurt parfait with oats, banana, honey; handful of nuts)
  - Pre-lift snack: 25 g protein + 60 g carbs (whey + bagel/jam)
  - Post-lift lunch: 45 g protein + 120 g carbs + 20 g fat (rice bowl with lean meat, veggies, olive oil)
  - Afternoon: 25 g protein + 60 g carbs (cottage cheese + fruit + granola; or smoothie)
  - Dinner: 30 g protein + 50 g carbs + 20 g fat (salmon, potatoes, salad with dressing)

Step 5: Hydration and electrolytes
- Fluids: 30–40 ml/kg/day (2.4–3.2 L at 80 kg) plus 500–1,000 ml per hour of training.
- Sodium: 1–2 g extra on training days (via salt or electrolyte mix), especially with added running.
- Include potassium/magnesium from food (fruit, potatoes, leafy greens, dairy) or a light electrolyte.

Step 6: Micronutrients and supplements
- Omega-3s: 1–2 g EPA/DHA/day (fatty fish 2–3x/week or fish oil).
- Vitamin D: Per bloods; if unknown, 1,000–2,000 IU/day is common.
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day (helps strength regain).
- Probiotic/yogurt/kefir: Support gut after illness.
- Fruit/veg: 5+ servings/day; include berries/citrus for appetite and antioxidants.

Step 7: Appetite and digestion strategies
- Use liquid calories: smoothies with milk/yogurt, oats, fruit, honey.
- Choose lower-fiber carb sources around training (rice, potatoes, pasta, sourdough, ripe fruit).
- Add calorie boosters if intake lags: olive oil, nut butters, honey, dried fruit.
- Keep meals palatable and warm; avoid very fatty or spicy foods pre-training.

Progress checks
- Weigh 3–4 mornings/week after bathroom, before food; use weekly average.
- Targets met if:
  - Bodyweight +0.4–0.6 kg/week
  - Training energy stable, RHR within baseline +0–5 bpm, good sleep
- If fatigue creeps up, first add 30–60 g carbs/day before raising fats; if still sluggish, increase total calories by +150–200 kcal/day.

This framework restores the lost 4 kg over several weeks while fueling the reconditioning block and keeping digestion and recovery on track.

Short answer: It’s not reasonable to jump straight back to pre-illness loads after 3 weeks off with recent flu and current deconditioning (fatigue history + 4 kg weight loss). Even if he “feels fine” today, strength, tendon stiffness, work capacity, and immune recovery lag behind perceived energy. The safer, faster way back to baseline is a brief ramp that re-establishes tolerance and confirms readiness over several sessions.

Why not jump to prior loads now
- Detraining window: After ~2–3 weeks off, neural efficiency holds better than tissue tolerance. Bar speed might feel okay while tendons, passive tissues, and small stabilizers aren’t ready for prior peak loads/volumes.
- Illness impact: Flu and weight loss reduce glycogen, plasma volume, and muscle cross-sectional area. Even at equal RPE, recovery debt is higher.
- Injury risk: Rapid spike in intensity/volume is a common trigger for adductor/hamstring strains, biceps tendon/pec irritation, and low-back flare-ups in the first week back.
- False readiness: One “good energy” day doesn’t confirm robustness across a full training week.

A pragmatic compromise if he’s adamant
- Keep Week 1’s structure but allow slightly higher top sets to test readiness, with strict exit ramps.
- Main lifts this week:
  - Bench: Single or double at RPE 7 (~80% of pre-illness) after controlled warm-ups; then 3–4 x 3–4 at ~70–75%. If speed slows >15% or technique wobbles, drop 5–7% or end there.
  - Squat: Same approach—top set x 3 @ RPE 7, back-offs 3 x 3–4 @ 70–75%.
  - Deadlift: More conservative—top set x 2–3 @ RPE 7, then 3 x 2–3 @ 70–72.5%. Pulls tend to expose fatigue quickest.
- Keep assistance at moderate volume (2–3 sets) and avoid failure.
- Maintain easy aerobic work only (Zone 2). No tempos or hills this week.

Objective guardrails (use these to make the call, not feelings alone)
- Resting HR and HRV: Only proceed with heavier work if RHR is within 0–5 bpm of baseline and sleep has been solid for 3 nights.
- Warm-up speed: If last ramp-up set at ~70% is slower than pre-illness norms or technique feels shaky, cap the day at ~70–75% and do volume there.
- Bar speed cap: If rep 2 of a top set drops below ~0.3–0.35 m/s (or subjectively “grindy”), stop 1–2 reps early and do not load up.
- Next-day check: DOMS and joint/tendon feel should be mild. If back, adductors, pec/shoulder are sore or “twingey” the next morning, reduce the following session’s load/sets.

What “starting at pre-illness loads” would actually look like—and why it’s a trap
- Pre-illness working sets likely lived around 75–85% for strength work and higher accessory volumes. Hitting those right away increases weekly tonnage and intensity >30–50% versus the reconditioning plan. That’s a classic acute:chronic spike, which correlates with soft-tissue issues and stalled recovery, especially with concurrent run reintroduction.
- Even if he survives Day 1, Days 3–5 usually expose the mismatch: tight hip flexors, adductors, cranky elbows/pec tendon, and fatigue that blunts Week 2 progress.

Best path to get him back fastest
- Use the planned 3-week ramp (or the compromise above). Most athletes are back lifting 80–90%+ by end of Week 3 and ready to touch singles at RPE 7–8. This avoids a setback week.
- Tie loads to performance: If Week 1 feels easy and markers look good, accelerate within the plan:
  - Bench Day 1: 62.5–67.5 kg for 4 x 5; if effortless, bump 2.5 kg on last 1–2 sets.
  - Squat Day 2: 90–95 kg for 4 x 5 if warm-ups fly.
  - Deadlift Day 5: 110–115 kg for 4 x 3 if positions are pristine.
- Then in Week 2, push top sets toward ~75% (RPE 7–8) and in Week 3 toward ~80–82% (RPE 8–9), confirming return to baseline without overreaching.

How to sell it to him
- “Two weeks of smart loading beats two months rehabbing a tweak.”
- “You’ll touch 80–85% within 10–14 days; we just need a few sessions to reload the system.”
- Show him the objective checkpoints above so it feels performance-driven, not arbitrary caution.

Bottom line
- Skipping Week 1 and jumping to pre-illness loads is a high-risk, low-upside move after flu + 3 weeks off + 4 kg loss.
- If he insists, use the compromise with top sets around RPE 7 and tight guardrails, keep volume modest, and reassess after each session. This preserves momentum while minimizing downside.

Use a simple return-to-full-intensity checklist that blends objective metrics, in-session performance, and recovery between sessions. When most boxes are green for 7–10 days, he’s ready to resume normal heavy work (85–92%+ and usual hypertrophy volume).

1) Daily readiness markers
- Resting HR: Back at personal baseline (within 0–5 bpm) for 5–7 consecutive mornings.
- Sleep: 3–5+ nights of normal duration/quality with no unusual nighttime awakenings.
- Subjective fatigue: ≤3/10 most mornings; no afternoon crashes.
- Appetite and weight: Appetite normal; weekly weight trend rising toward target (+0.4–0.6 kg/week during reconditioning) without GI issues.

2) Aerobic signs (since running is back)
- Easy run HR/RPE: At his pre-illness easy pace, HR drift minimal (<5–7 bpm rise over 30–40 min) and RPE 3–4.
- No chest tightness, breathlessness, or lingering cough with easy runs; recovery feels normal next day (no heavy legs beyond mild).

3) In-gym performance indicators
- Bar speed and RPE alignment:
  - Warm-up sets at ~60–70% move like they used to (snappy, no technique compensation).
  - Top sets at RPE 7–8 land near expected loads (≈75–82% of former max) with consistent bar speed and no grind.
- Volume tolerance:
  - Can complete planned main-lift volume (e.g., 12–20 working reps in squat/bench/deadlift across sets) without form drift.
  - Accessories at usual volumes (2–4 sets, 6–12 reps) don’t create excessive pump or shaky fatigue.
- DOMS/joint response:
  - Next-day soreness is mild/moderate and resolves within 24–48 hours.
  - No focal tendon/joint irritation (pec/biceps, adductor/hip flexor, low back) across a full training week.

4) Recovery between sessions
- Strength carryover: Performance on the second upper and lower day of the week is equal or slightly better than the first (no midweek drop-offs).
- Heart rate recovery: HR drops quickly between sets again; breathing normalizes within 60–90 seconds after hard sets.
- Energy on combined days: If a run and lift land within 24 hours, he still feels competent in the second session.

5) Load checkpoints (practical test)
- Session test 1: After warm-ups, hit a single at RPE 7–8 in each lift with clean form and crisp speed:
  - Bench ~80–85 kg
  - Squat ~110–120 kg
  - Deadlift ~135–145 kg
  If these feel smooth and repeatable, proceed to back-off work without fatigue spike.
- Session test 2 (48–72 hours later): Repeat a similar exposure or complete a normal volume day (e.g., 4 x 3–5 at 75–80%) and feel recovered the next day. If both tests pass, green light to resume full-intensity training the following week.

6) Red flags that mean “not yet”
- RHR consistently +8–10 bpm vs baseline, poor sleep, or afternoon crashes.
- RPE creep (sets at 70–75% feel like RPE 8–9) or bar path getting wobbly.
- DOMS persisting >48 hours, or tendon/joint hot spots.
- HR drift >10–12 bpm on easy runs, or unusual breathlessness.

When you flip the switch
- Reintroduce intensity first, then volume:
  - Week A: Touch 85–90% for singles/doubles at RPE 8–9 with normal back-off volume.
  - Week B: Restore full accessory/hypertrophy volume and, if desired, small doses of higher-intensity running (tempos/strides), watching for any regression in the markers above.

This framework gives you clear, objective signals to move from reconditioning to full-intensity work while minimizing risk of setbacks.

Great idea. Here’s a safe, performance-focused 1RM test protocol slotted into the back half of Week 3, with exact day placement, warm-ups, load jumps, and contingency rules. Goal: get true or near-true maxes without derailing recovery so you can program off updated numbers next block.

Schedule (Week 3)
- Mon: Upper A (as planned)
- Tue: Lower A (as planned)
- Wed: Light recovery (as planned)
- Thu: Bench 1RM test + light upper back/shoulders
- Fri: Deadlift 1RM test + light quads/hinge/core

- Sun: Full rest

Why this order: Bench first (least systemic fatigue), deadlift next (so legs are fresh), squat last (you’ll still have pop after Fri if you keep deadlift volume low).

General test rules
- Stop each lift when you hit RPE 9.5–10 or bar speed clearly slows to a grind. One attempt at true max is plenty; no more than 3 “heavy” attempts at ≥90% on any day.
- If any warm-up rep feels off or pain emerges, cap the day at a heavy single @ RPE 8–9 and call that your “training max” for programming.
- Between heavy attempts: 3–5 minutes rest for bench, 4–6 minutes for squat/deadlift.

Warm-up template (all three lifts)
- General: 5–7 min easy cardio + dynamic mobility + 2–3 activation sets.
- Barbell warm-ups:
  - Empty bar x 8–10
  - ~40% x 5
  - ~55% x 3
  - ~70% x 2
  - ~80% x 1
  - ~87–90% x 1 (confidence single)
  - Then attempts

Plates and attempt selection
Bench press (Thu)
- Target fresh attempts: 1st: 85 kg (confidence single), 2nd: 92.5 kg, 3rd: 97.5–102.5 kg based on bar speed.
- Example flow (adjust to RPE):
  - 80% (80 kg) x 1
  - 87–90% (87.5–90 kg) x 1
  - Attempt 1: 92.5 kg (should be RPE 8–9)
  - Attempt 2: If fast, 97.5 kg
  - Attempt 3: If 97.5 flies, go 100–102.5 kg; if 92.5 was slow, take 95 kg and stop there.
- Back-off: Optional 2–3 x 2 @ ~82.5% if you want volume (only if feeling great). Otherwise, do light accessories:
  - Chest-supported row 3 x 6–8
  - Face pulls 2 x 12–15
  - Triceps pressdowns 2 x 10–12

Deadlift (Fri)
- Target fresh attempts: 1st: 150 kg, 2nd: 160–165 kg, 3rd: 170–180 kg depending on speed and grip.
- Example flow:
  - 80% (136 kg) x 1
  - 87–90% (148–153 kg) x 1
  - Attempt 1: 160 kg
  - Attempt 2: If clean, 170 kg
  - Attempt 3: If 170 is snappy, 175–180 kg; if 160 was slow, 165 and stop.
- Back-off: None required; if you want work, do 2 x 2 @ 75–80% or skip and hit:
  - Single-leg RDL 2 x 6/side
  - Stir-the-pot/ab wheel 2–3 sets

Squat (Sat)
- Target fresh attempts: 1st: 120–125 kg, 2nd: 130–135 kg, 3rd: 140–150 kg depending on speed.
- Example flow:
  - 80% (112 kg) x 1
  - 87–90% (122–126 kg) x 1
  - Attempt 1: 130 kg
  - Attempt 2: If tidy, 140 kg
  - Attempt 3: If 140 is smooth, 145–150 kg; if 130 felt grindy, 135 and stop.
- Back-off: Optional 2 x 2 @ ~80% only if energy is high; otherwise:
  - Split squat 2 x 6/side
  - Calf raises 2 x 10–12

Autoregulation and safety guardrails
- Hard cap: If any confidence single (≈87–90%) feels ≥RPE 9, abandon maxing and take a solid single @ RPE 8–9 to set a training max (TM = that load).
- Bar speed cue (no device needed): If the rep takes >3 seconds through the concentric or path gets wobbly, treat it as near-max and stop there.
- Pain: Any sharp pain or focal tendon discomfort = end max attempts immediately.
- Volume discipline: Keep accessories minimal this week to preserve CNS and joints.

Fueling and logistics
- Night before: Carb-heavy dinner; hydrate well; 1–2 g extra sodium if you don’t have BP issues.
- Pre-test (60–120 min): 30–80 g carbs + 20–40 g protein, low fat/fiber.
- Caffeine: Usual dose; don’t exceed normal to avoid jitters.
- Warm-up timing: Take your time. Total session 60–75 min is fine.

How to use the results
- If you hit true 1RMs: Program next block off 88–92% as your training max (keeps headroom).
  - Example if you hit: Bench 100, Squat 145, Deadlift 175
    - Set TMs at 90%: Bench 90, Squat 130, Deadlift 158 (or round logically).
- If you only reach strong singles @ RPE 8–9: Estimate 1RM using E1RM and set TM at ~90% of E1RM.
  - E1RM quick calc: Load x (1 + reps x 0.03) for submax sets, or use RPE charts: a single @ RPE 8 ≈ 92% of 1RM.

Post-testing recovery and transition
- After Sat squat test: Easy 20–30 min walk and light mobility.
- Next week (Week 4): Deload the first half slightly (reduce accessory volume 20–30%) or take two easy days, then start the new program using the updated TMs.

This structure lets you capture real numbers with minimal risk, at the exact point in the block where readiness is highest.

  - Attempt 2: If clean, 170 kg
  - Attempt 3: If 170 is snappy, 175–180 kg; if 160 was slow, 165 and stop
- Back-off: None required; if any, 2 x 2 @ 75–80% or skip and do single-leg RDL 2 x 6/side + core (stir-the-pot/ab wheel 2–3 sets)

Day 6 – Squat 1RM Test (Sat)
- Warm-up:
  - Bar x 8–10
  - 40% (56 kg) x 5
  - 55% (77 kg) x 3
  - 70% (98 kg) x 2
  - 80% (112 kg) x 1
  - 87–90% (122–126 kg) x 1
- Attempts:
  - Attempt 1: 130 kg
  - Attempt 2: If tidy, 140 kg
  - Attempt 3: If 140 is smooth, 145–150 kg; if 130 felt grindy, 135 and stop
- Back-off (optional): 2 x 2 @ ~80% only if energy is high
- Post: Easy 20–30 min walk and light mobility
Day 7 – Rest (Sun)

1RM test safety and rules
- Hard cap: If the confidence single at ~87–90% feels ≥RPE 9, stop maxing and take a solid single @ RPE 8–9 as the training max
- Attempts: No more than three ≥90% attempts per lift
- Bar speed: If the concentric is a clear grind (>3 seconds) or path wobbles, treat as near-max and stop
- Pain: Any sharp or focal tendon pain = terminate attempts

Using the results (programming next block)
- If true 1RMs achieved: Set training maxes (TM) at ~88–92% of tested 1RM for the next mesocycle
- If only strong singles @ RPE 8–9 achieved: Estimate 1RM via E1RM and use ~90% of E1RM as TM

Running progression (integrated)
- Week 1 total: 6–8 km
  - Wed: 20–25 min easy (RPE 3–4), ~3–4 km
  - Sat: 25–30 min easy (RPE 3–4), ~3–4 km
- Week 2 total: 8–10 km
  - Wed: 30–35 min easy (RPE 3–4), ~4–5.5 km
  - Sat: 25–30 min easy (RPE 3–4), ~3–4.5 km
- Week 3 total: 10–12 km
  - Wed: 20–30 min easy only (keep stress low before testing)
  - Sat: No run (squat test day). Optional 20–30 min walk after testing
  - Strides: Move 4–6 x 15–20 s relaxed strides to the following week (post-testing) to avoid interference

Pacing and monitoring for runs
- Keep all runs conversational (talk test) or ~70–78% max HR
- Red flags: Chest tightness, unusual breathlessness, HR drift >10–12 bpm at steady pace—cut session and report

Nutrition to regain 4 kg and support training (3 weeks)
- Calories:
  - Week 1: ~33–36 kcal/kg/day
  - Weeks 2–3: ~35–38 kcal/kg/day (adjust +150–200 kcal/day if weekly gain <0.4 kg; trim if >0.8 kg with bloat)
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day (aim ~2.0 g/kg)
- Carbs: 4–6 g/kg/day; higher on lift/run days, front-load around training
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day, mostly unsaturated; include omega-3s (1–2 g EPA/DHA/day)
- Hydration/electrolytes: 30–40 ml/kg/day water; add 1–2 g sodium on training days
- Peri-workout:
  - Pre-lift: 30–80 g carbs + 20–40 g protein (60–120 min prior)
  - Intra (optional >75 min): 20–30 g carbs + electrolytes
  - Post: 30–50 g protein + 60–100 g carbs
  - Run days: +30–60 g carbs pre, +40–80 g post
- Practical strategies: Use liquid calories if appetite lags; choose lower-fiber carbs around sessions; add easy calorie boosters (olive oil, nut butters, honey)

Readiness and “return-to-full-intensity” checkpoints
- Daily: RHR back within 0–5 bpm of baseline for 5–7 days; sleep solid; fatigue ≤3/10; appetite/weight trending up
- Aerobic: Easy runs show minimal HR drift (<5–7 bpm over 30–40 min) at RPE 3–4; no respiratory symptoms
- Gym performance:
  - 60–70% warm-ups move like baseline
  - Top sets at RPE 7–8 land near 75–82% with consistent bar speed
  - Complete planned volume without form drift; next-day soreness resolves in 24–48 h
- Recovery between sessions: No midweek drop-offs; HR recovers between sets; feels capable even when a run and lift are within 24 h
- Red flags that delay progression: Persistent RHR +8–10 bpm, RPE creep at submax loads, DOMS >48 h, tendon/joint hot spots, or abnormal breathlessness on easy runs

Contingency: “Pushy client” compromise in Week 1 (if insisting on heavier work)
- Keep Week 1 structure but allow a top set at RPE ~7 on main lifts (bench/squat x3–4; deadlift x2–3), with -8–10% back-offs and strict exit ramps
- Maintain easy running only; no tempos or hills
- If any joint/tendon irritation or fatigue spike, revert to the lighter percentages immediately

This plan restores strength, mileage, and bodyweight methodically, then captures accurate 1RMs at the end of Week 3 so you can program the next block off real, current numbers with minimal risk.

Here’s the complete 3-week reconditioning program with all adjustments integrated: precise Week 1 working numbers for the big lifts, concurrent run progression back to 10k/week, nutrition targets for weight regain, readiness criteria, and a Week 3 1RM testing schedule.

Structure
- Weekly split: Upper A / Lower A / Active Recovery + Easy Run / Upper B / Lower B / Easy Run / Rest
- Lifting focus: Submaximal start, volume-first ramp, sharpen intensity by Week 3
- Running: Rebuild easy mileage only in Weeks 1–2, add strides in Week 3
- Nutrition: Modest surplus to regain 0.4–0.6 kg/week
- Readiness: Daily checks; clear criteria to return to full intensity
- End of block: 1RM testing Thu–Sat of Week 3 to set new training maxes

Warm-up (every lift day)
- 5–8 min easy cardio (bike/row), nasal breathing
- Dynamic mobility: T-spine rotations, hip flexor stretch, 90/90 hips, ankle rocks, band pull-aparts (4–6 reps each)
- Movement prep: 2–3 ramp-up sets per main lift, RPE 4–6; prioritize crisp bar speed and bracing

Autoregulation guardrails
- If morning RHR is up >8–10 bpm from baseline, poor sleep, or high fatigue: reduce top set 2–5% and drop one back-off set
- If rep 2 of a top set is grindy or technique wobbles: stop 1–2 reps early; don’t chase percentages

Week 1: Reintroduce patterns, confirm tolerance, rebuild easy volume
- RPE target: ~6–7 (3–4 reps in reserve)
- Conditioning: Two easy runs (6–8 km total for the week), one mobility session

Day 1 – Upper A
- Bench press: 4 x 5 @ 60–65% (RPE 6)
  - Pre-illness 1RM = 100 kg; use 60–65 kg (start 60–62.5 kg, up to 65 kg if snappy)
- One-arm DB row: 3 x 8–10/side (RPE 7)
- Incline DB bench: 3 x 8 (RPE 7)
- Neutral lat pulldown: 3 x 10 (RPE 7)
- Cable external rotation + band pull-aparts: 2 x 12–15 each
- Core: Dead bug 3 x 8/side

Day 2 – Lower A
- Back squat: 4 x 5 @ 60–65% (RPE 6)
  - Pre-illness 1RM = 140 kg; use 85–90 kg (92.5 kg if very easy)
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8 (RPE 6–7)
- Split squat (RFESS if tolerated): 3 x 8/side (RPE 7)
- Leg curl: 3 x 10 (RPE 7)
- Standing calf raise: 3 x 12
- Breathing cooldown: 3–4 min nasal breathing, 90/90 hip lift

Day 3 – Active Recovery + Easy Run
- Easy run: 20–25 min at conversational effort (RPE 3–4), ~3–4 km
- Mobility circuit: 10–15 min (hips, T-spine, ankles)
- Optional: 10–15 min walk later in day

Day 4 – Upper B
- Overhead press (BB or DB): 4 x 5 (RPE 6)
- Pull-up (weighted or assisted): 4 x 5 (RPE 6–7) or 4 x 6–8 bodyweight
- Close-grip bench or dips (assisted as needed): 3 x 8 (RPE 7)
- Chest-supported row: 3 x 8–10 (RPE 7)
- Face pulls: 2 x 12–15
- Farmer carry: 3 x 20–30 m

Day 5 – Lower B
- Deadlift (conventional): 4 x 3 @ ~60–65% (RPE 6)
  - Pre-illness 1RM = 170 kg; use 105–110 kg (100–105 kg if under-recovered)
- Front squat or tempo goblet squat (3-1-1): 3 x 6–8 (RPE 7)
- Hip thrust: 3 x 8 (RPE 7)
- Reverse lunge: 2–3 x 8/side
- Plank: 3 x 30–45 s

Day 6 – Easy Run (and optional light recovery)
- Easy run: 25–30 min at conversational effort (RPE 3–4), ~3–4 km
- Optional light mobility

Day 7 – Rest

Week 2: Add a controlled top set, keep accessories moderate, maintain easy aerobic base
- RPE target: 6–8; introduce one top set at RPE 7–8, then back-offs
- Conditioning: Two easy runs (8–10 km total)

Day 1 – Upper A
- Bench press: Top set 1 x 4 @ ~70–75% (RPE 7–8; ~70–75 kg), then 3 x 4 @ -8–10% (RPE 6–7; ~62.5–67.5 kg)
- One-arm DB row: 4 x 8–10 (RPE 7–8)
- Incline DB bench: 3 x 8 (RPE 7–8)
- Wide-grip pulldown or pull-ups: 3 x 8–10
- Cable Y raise + external rotations: 2 x 12–15
- Pallof press: 3 x 10/side

Day 2 – Lower A
- Back squat: Top set 1 x 4 @ ~70–75% (RPE 7–8; ~100–105 kg), then 3 x 4 @ -8–10% (90–97.5 kg)
- RDL: 3 x 6–8 (RPE 7)
- Split squat: 3 x 8/side (RPE 7–8)
- Leg curl: 3 x 10–12
- Calf raise: 3 x 12–15

Day 3 – Active Recovery + Easy Run
- Easy run: 30–35 min (RPE 3–4), ~4–5.5 km
- Mobility and breath work: 10–15 min

Day 4 – Upper B
- Overhead press: Top set 1 x 4 (RPE 7–8), then 3 x 4 back-offs (-8–10%)
- Pull-ups: 4 x 5–6 (light weight if easy; bodyweight to RPE 7 if not)
- Close-grip bench or dips: 3 x 6–8 (RPE 7–8)
- Chest-supported row: 3 x 8–10
- Face pulls or rear-delt fly: 2 x 12–15
- Suitcase carry: 3 x 20–30 m/side

Day 5 – Lower B
- Deadlift: Top set 1 x 3 @ ~70–75% (RPE 7–8; ~120–127.5 kg), then 3 x 3 @ -8–10% (110–115 kg)
- Front squat (or tempo goblet): 3 x 5–6 (RPE 7–8)
- Hip thrust: 3 x 8 (RPE 7–8)
- Reverse lunge: 2–3 x 8/side
- Stir-the-pot or ab wheel: 3 x 6–10

Day 6 – Easy Run
- Easy run: 25–30 min (RPE 3–4), ~3–4.5 km
Day 7 – Rest

Week 3: Sharpen intensity, reduce accessory volume, test and then 1RM
- RPE target: 7–9 on top sets; clean technique
- Conditioning: One early-week easy run only (20–30 min), then focus on testing

Day 1 – Upper A (Mon)
- Bench press: 1–2 top sets x 3 @ ~77–82% (RPE 8–9; ~77.5–82.5 kg), then 2 x 3 @ -8–10% (70–75 kg)
- One-arm DB row: 3 x 6–8 (RPE 8)
- Incline DB bench: 2 x 6–8 (RPE 8)
- Pull-ups or pulldown: 2–3 x 6–8 (RPE 8)
- Light shoulder health: 1–2 x 12–15

Day 2 – Lower A (Tue)
- Back squat: 1–2 top sets x 3 @ ~77–82% (RPE 8–9; ~107.5–115 kg), then 2 x 3 back-offs (97.5–105 kg)
- RDL: 3 x 5–6 (RPE 7–8)
- Split squat: 2 x 6–8/side
- Calf raise: 2 x 10–12

Day 3 – Light Recovery + Easy Run (Wed)
- Easy run: 20–30 min (RPE 3–4), keep it flat; stop if fatigue spikes
- Mobility: 10 min

Day 4 – Bench 1RM Test (Thu)
- Warm-up:
  - Bar x 8–10
  - 40% (40 kg) x 5
  - 55% (55 kg) x 3
  - 70% (70 kg) x 2
  - 80% (80 kg) x 1
  - 87–90% (87.5–90 kg) x 1 (confidence single)
- Attempts:
  - Attempt 1: 92.5 kg
  - Attempt 2: If fast, 97.5 kg
  - Attempt 3: If 97.5 is smooth, 100–102.5 kg; if 92.5 was slow, 95 kg and stop
- Back-off (optional): 2–3 x 2 @ ~82.5% only if feeling great
- Light accessories: Chest-supported row 3 x 6–8; Face pulls 2 x 12–15; Triceps pressdowns 2 x 10–12

Day 5 – Deadlift 1RM Test (Fri)
- Warm-up:
  - Bar/warm-up pulls
  - 40% (68 kg) x 5
  - 55% (95 kg) x 3
  - 70% (119 kg) x 2
  - 80% (136 kg) x 1
  - 87–90% (148–153 kg) x 1
- Attempts:
  - Attempt 1: 160 kg
  - Attempt 2: If clean, 170 kg
  - Attempt 3: If 170 is snappy, 175–180 kg; if 160 was slow, 165 and stop
- Back-off: None required; if any, 2 x 2 @ 75–80% or skip and do single-leg RDL 2 x 6/side + core (stir-the-pot/ab wheel 2–3 sets)

Day 6 – Squat 1RM Test (Sat)
- Warm-up:
  - Bar x 8–10
  - 40% (56 kg) x 5
  - 55% (77 kg) x 3
  - 70% (98 kg) x 2
  - 80% (112 kg) x 1
  - 87–90% (122–126 kg) x 1
- Attempts:
  - Attempt 1: 130 kg
  - Attempt 2: If tidy, 140 kg
  - Attempt 3: If 140 is smooth, 145–150 kg; if 130 felt grindy, 135 and stop
- Back-off (optional): 2 x 2 @ ~80% only if energy is high
- Post: Easy 20–30 min walk and light mobility
Day 7 – Rest (Sun)

1RM test safety and rules
- Hard cap: If the confidence single at ~87–90% feels ≥RPE 9, stop maxing and take a solid single @ RPE 8–9 as the training max
- Attempts: No more than three ≥90% attempts per lift
- Bar speed: If the concentric is a clear grind (>3 seconds) or path wobbles, treat as near-max and stop
- Pain: Any sharp or focal tendon pain = terminate attempts

Using the results (programming next block)
- If true 1RMs achieved: Set training maxes (TM) at ~88–92% of tested 1RM for the next mesocycle
- If only strong singles @ RPE 8–9 achieved: Estimate 1RM via E1RM and use ~90% of E1RM as TM

Running progression (integrated)
- Week 1 total: 6–8 km
  - Wed: 20–25 min easy (RPE 3–4), ~3–4 km
  - Sat: 25–30 min easy (RPE 3–4), ~3–4 km
- Week 2 total: 8–10 km
  - Wed: 30–35 min easy (RPE 3–4), ~4–5.5 km
  - Sat: 25–30 min easy (RPE 3–4), ~3–4.5 km
- Week 3 total: 10–12 km
  - Wed: 20–30 min easy only (keep stress low before testing)
  - Sat: No run (squat test day). Optional 20–30 min walk after testing
  - Strides: Move 4–6 x 15–20 s relaxed strides to the following week (post-testing) to avoid interference

Pacing and monitoring for runs
- Keep all runs conversational (talk test) or ~70–78% max HR
- Red flags: Chest tightness, unusual breathlessness, HR drift >10–12 bpm at steady pace—cut session and report

Nutrition to regain 4 kg and support training (3 weeks)
- Calories:
  - Week 1: ~33–36 kcal/kg/day
  - Weeks 2–3: ~35–38 kcal/kg/day (adjust +150–200 kcal/day if weekly gain <0.4 kg; trim if >0.8 kg with bloat)
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day (aim ~2.0 g/kg)
- Carbs: 4–6 g/kg/day; higher on lift/run days, front-load around training
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day, mostly unsaturated; include omega-3s (1–2 g EPA/DHA/day)
- Hydration/electrolytes: 30–40 ml/kg/day water; add 1–2 g sodium on training days
- Peri-workout:
  - Pre-lift: 30–80 g carbs + 20–40 g protein (60–120 min prior)
  - Intra (optional >75 min): 20–30 g carbs + electrolytes
  - Post: 30–50 g protein + 60–100 g carbs
  - Run days: +30–60 g carbs pre, +40–80 g post
- Practical strategies: Use liquid calories if appetite lags; choose lower-fiber carbs around sessions; add easy calorie boosters (olive oil, nut butters, honey)

Readiness and “return-to-full-intensity” checkpoints
- Daily: RHR back within 0–5 bpm of baseline for 5–7 days; sleep solid; fatigue ≤3/10; appetite/weight trending up
- Aerobic: Easy runs show minimal HR drift (<5–7 bpm over 30–40 min) at RPE 3–4; no respiratory symptoms
- Gym performance:
  - 60–70% warm-ups move like baseline
  - Top sets at RPE 7–8 land near 75–82% with consistent bar speed
  - Complete planned volume without form drift; next-day soreness resolves in 24–48 h
- Recovery between sessions: No midweek drop-offs; HR recovers between sets; feels capable even when a run and lift are within 24 h
- Red flags that delay progression: Persistent RHR +8–10 bpm, RPE creep at submax loads, DOMS >48 h, tendon/joint hot spots, or abnormal breathlessness on easy runs

Contingency: “Pushy client” compromise in Week 1 (if insisting on heavier work)
- Keep Week 1 structure but allow a top set at RPE ~7 on main lifts (bench/squat x3–4; deadlift x2–3), with -8–10% back-offs and strict exit ramps
- Maintain easy running only; no tempos or hills
- If any joint/tendon irritation or fatigue spike, revert to the lighter percentages immediately

This plan restores strength, mileage, and bodyweight methodically, then captures accurate 1RMs at the end of Week 3 so you can program the next block off real, current numbers with minimal risk.
